question.problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the points $(0,-1)$ and $(3,5).$
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{5-(-1)}{3-0} \\  & =\frac{6}{3} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The coordinates of the $y$-intercept are always $(0,b).$ We know that the line passes through the point $(0,-1),$ so the $y$-intercept is $b=-1.$  

Substituting the slope $m=2$ and the $y$-intercept $b=-1$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=2x-1.
$$
